FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard (First Revision) was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by 
the Gas Cylinders Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council. 


This standard was first published in 1968. This standard is revised to incorporate the latest technological 
development taken place. In this revision following modification has been incorporated: 


a) Strength of connection, 
b) Type tests: 


1) Hydrostatic test, 

2) Endurance test, 

3) Low and high temperature tests, and 

4) Mechanical strength of connection. 
c) Routine tests: 


1) Finish, 
2) Dimensions (screw threads), 
3) Inlet sealing, 
4) Soundness, 
5) Performance, and 
6) Test for excess flow device, if provided. 
In the preparation of this standard considerable assistance has been derived from the following: 


a) IS 9798 : 2013 ‘Low pressure regulators for use with liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) — Specification’, 

b) EN 12864 : 2001 ‘Low pressure non-adjustable regulators having a maximum pressure of less than or 
equal to 200 m bar with a capacity of less than or equal to 4 kg/h and their associated safety devices for 
butane, propane or their mixtures’, and 

c) EN 13785 : 2005 ‘Regulators with a capacity of up to and including 100 kg/h, having a maximum 
nominal outlet pressure of up to and including 4 bar, other than those covered by EN 12864 and their 
associated safety devices for butane, propane or their mixtures’ 


Pressures indicated in the various requirements/clauses of this standard are gauge pressure unless otherwise 
stated. 


While implementing this standard compliance with statutory regulations shall be ensured. 
The composition of the Committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given in Annex L. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


Indian Standard 


VARIABLE HIGH PRESSURE REGULATORS (VHPR) 
FOR USE WITH LIQUEFIED PETROLEUM GASES — 
SPECIFICATION 


( First Revision ) 


1 SCOPE 


1.1 This standard specifies materials, construction, 
performance, safety and testing requirements for 
“variable high pressure regulators (VHPR)” for use with 
liquefied petroleum gases (butane, propane and their 
mixtures) in vapour phase above 4.903 kN/m? 150 gf/ 
cm? or 500 mm water column (WC)], outlet pressure 
and up to 686.42 kN/m? (7 kg/cm?) outlet pressure. 


NOTE — Generally LPG appliances are being designed to 
operate at a pressure of 1kgf/em?, but specialized equipment 
may call for use of still higher pressures. 


1.2 This standard does not cover rules for installation 
of regulators during actual use and reference should 
be made to applicable rules. 


2 REFERENCES 


The standards listed in Annex A contain provisions 
which, through reference in this text, constitute 
provisions of the standard. At the time of publication, 
the editions indicated were valid. All standards are 
subject to revision, and parties to agreements based on 
this standard are encouraged to investigate the 
possibility of applying the most recent editions of the 
standards listed in Annex A. 


3 TERMINOLOGY 


For the purpose of this standard, the following 
definitions shall apply : 


3.1 Commercial Butane — A hydrocarbon product 
composed predominantly of butanes (n and iso), 
butylenes or their mixtures of maximum vapour 
pressure of 980 kPa (10 kgf/cm’). 


3.2 Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) — A 
hydrocarbon product composed predominantly of a 
mixture of butanes (n and iso), and/or butylenes with 
propane and/or propylene of maximum vapour pressure 
of 1 653 kPa (16.87 kgf/cm2 at 65°C. 


3.3 Commercial Propane Gas — A hydrocarbon 
product composed predominantly of propane, 
propylene or their mixtures, of, maximum vapour 
pressure of 2 550 kPa (26 kgf/cm’). 


3.4 Variable High Pressure Regulator (VHPR) — 
A regulator for use with LPG in the vapour phase, 
designed and manufactured to deliver at its outlet 
regulated pressures above 4.903 kN/m? [50 gf/cm? or 
500 mm water column (WC)] and upto 686.42 kN/m? 
(7 kg/cm?) outlet pressure for obtaining and 
maintaining any desired outlet pressure within the 
designed range of outlet pressures and provided 
externally, with simple adjustment means, so that the 
user can set desired outlet pressure within the designed 
outlet pressure range. 


3.5 Operating Temperatures — The range of 
temperatures between which the VHPR shall be 
designed to operate, depending upon the gas for which 
the VHPR has be designed, but shall at least be -20°C 
to 65°C. 


3.6 Operating Inlet Pressures — The range of inlet 
pressures (at regulator inlet or cylinder valve outlet) 
within which the VHPR is capable of delivering the 
guaranteed flow, at any variably set outlet pressures 
within the designed outlet pressure range (with clean 
filter). 


3.7 Designed Outlet Pressures — The range of 
regulated pressures obtainable from the outlet of the 
VHPR for any inlet pressure (within operating inlet 
pressures) when using the gas for which the VHPR 
has been designed. 


3.8 Guaranteed Flow Rate — The minimum assured 
stable outflow in m”/h, that a VHPR will supply at any 
setting and any inlet pressure. 


3.8 Excess Flow Check Valve — A device integral 
with the VHPR which shut-off the gas flow for any 
outflows greater by a percentage than the maximum 
guaranteed flow. 


3.9 Inlet Sealing — Preventing inflow of gas from 
inlet passage of VHPR with the VHPR operating handle 
switched OFF. 


3.10 Lock-up Pressure — The maximum pressure 
obtainable at no flow for all values of inlet 
pressures. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


4 MATERIALS 


4.1 All component parts shall be manufactured from, 
or be treated with materials compatible with LPG as 
well as unaffected by chemical or thermal influences 
that may be encountered in normal use. Materials 
specified in IS 319, IS 410, IS 617, IS 742 and IS 6912 
are recommended for the manufacture of VHPRs; but 
other type of materials may be used provided the 
standards of performance, durability and safety of the 
VHPR are not lowered. 


4.1.1 Brass parts shall not be susceptible to season 
cracking. The susceptibility to season cracking shall 
be determined by the method given in IS 2305. 


4.2 Body and Cover 


The body and cover of all VHPRs shall be 
manufactured from zinc base/aluminum base alloys by 
pressure die-casting or from brass forging. Chemical 
composition of material of the pressure die cast body 
and cover of the VHPR shall conform to IS 742 or 
Grade 4600 of IS 617 or brass forged confirm to IS 
6912. 


4.2.1 Finish 


The body and the cover of the VHPR shall be painted 
or powder coated so as to resist the effect of 
atmospheric conditions to which the VHPR is exposed 
during its working life. The colour and type of finish 
shall be as agreed between the manufacturer and the 
customer. 


4.2.1.1 The surface finished components shall be 
subjected to test for corrosion resistance as per IS 9844. 
The evaluation of the finish shall be done as per the 
method given in 6 of IS 6009. 


4.2.1.2 The painted or powder coated surfaces shall 
be tested for adhesion of paint by the method described 
in Annex F. 


4.3 Diaphragm Material 


The material of the diaphragm shall be of synthetic 
rubber or other material equally suitable for the 
application and shall satisfy the following 
requirements. 


4.3.1 The material shall be free from porosity, pits and 
foreign particles and shall have a smooth non-tacky 
surface, with minimum talc or bloom. 


4.3.2 The material shall be impermeable to the test 
gas (see Annex B) at a pressure of 2.5 times the 
maximum outlet pressure obtainable from the VHPR 
when subjected to a suitable porosity test. 


4.3.3 The material shall be such that when the 
assembled VHPR is subjected to the test specified in 


Annex C, the diaphragm shall not pull out, or burst, at 
a pressure upto 981 kPa (10 kgf/cm’). 


4.3.4 The material shall be capable of withstanding a 
clamping pressure of 490 kPa (5 kgf/cm?) whereby the 
material itself or the substance with which the fabric 
layer has been impregnated shall not be pressed away, 
flow away, or be bruised or otherwise damaged. 


4.3.5 The material shall after immersion for 72 h in 
pentane or the liquid test gas (see Annex B), meet 
appropriate requirements specified in Annex E. After 
this test the material shall be still capable of meeting 
the flexibility requirements of 4.3.7. Change in 
hardness values before and after the immersion shall 
not exceed 15 IRHD [see IS 3400 (Part 2)]. 


NOTE — Tests at 4.3.1 to 4.3.5 are works batch tests. On initial 
selection of a diaphragm material, it shall also be tested in the 
test gas in the vapour phase for 72 h, and shall not show a 
weight or volume change greater than 15 percent. 


4.3.6 The material shall not show change of more than 
10 IRHD when subjected to ageing of 72 h at 70°C in 
accordance with the method prescribed in 3 or 4 of IS 
3400 (Part 4). 


NOTE — For guidance purpose, comparison of Shore A and 
IRHD hardness are given below: 


Shore A 30 40 50 60 70 
IRHD 28.9 395 50 60.5 70 


80 90 100 
80 89.5 100 


4.3.7 The material shall be such that the flexibility of 
the diaphragm shall not be impaired after samples of 
the same have recovered completely to ambient 
temperature from cooling to —20°C or heating to 65”C. 
For these tests, fully assembled VHPRs are cooled to 
—20”C or heated to 65°C and maintained at these 
temperatures for 10 min and then kept in atmosphere 
to recover completely to ambient temperature of its 
own (not by induced heating or cooling). After 
recovery, the performance of the VHPR shall be re- 
verified. The results shall be within acceptable limits. 


4.4 Valve Pad Material 


The material of the valve pad shall be of synthetic 
rubber or other material equally suitable for the 
application and shall satisfy the following 
requirements: 


4.4.1 The material shall be free from porosity, pits and 
foreign particles and shall have a smooth non-tacky 
surface with minimum talc or bloom. Also it shall have 
low compression set cold flow and creep 
characteristics. 


4.4.2 The material shall after immersion for 72 h in 
pentane or the liquid test gas (see Annex B), meet 
appropriate requirements specified in Annex E. Change 
in hardness values before and after the immersion shall 


not exceed 15 IRHD [see IS 3400 (Part 2)]. 


NOTE — Tests at 4.4.1 and 4.4.2 are works batch tests. On 
initial selection of valve pad material, it shall also be tested in 
the test gas in the vapour phase for 72 h and shall not show 
any volumetric shrinkage or volumetric increase greater than 
10 percent. The loss of plasticizers or other ingredient due to 
extraction shall not exceed 5 percent by weight. 


4.4.3 The material shall not show change of more than 
10 IRHD when subjected to ageing of 72 h at 70°C in 
accordance with the method prescribed in 3 or 4 of IS 
3400 (Part 4). 


4.4.4 The valve pad fitted in its housing shall be 
immersed in pentane or the test gas (see Annex B) in 
the vapour phase for 72 h after which the pad shall not 
show evidence of being forced out of position due to 
swelling or other causes. 


4.4.5 The hardness of the material shall not vary over 
a temperature range between the lowest temperature 
at which it will be required to function and 65°C to the 
extent that the performance of the VHPR fails to satisfy 
the requirements of 7.1. 


4.5 Seals, “O” Rings and Rubber Components 


Seals, “O” rings and rubber components other than 
diaphragm and valve pad shall be suitable for the 
application and shall satisfy the following 
requirements: 


4.5.1 The material shall be free from porosity, pits and 
foreign particles and shall have a smooth, non-tacky 
surface with minimum talc or bloom. 


4.5.2 The material shall after immersion for 72 h in 
pentane or the liquid test gas (see Annex B), meet 
appropriate requirements specified in Annex E. Change 
in hardness values before and after the Immersion shall 
not exceed 15 IRHD [see IS 3400 (Part 2)]. 


NOTE — The tests at 4.5.1 and 4.5.2 are work batch tests. On 
initial selection of a rubber component material, it shall also 
be tested in the test gas in the vapour phase for 72 h and shall 
not show a weight loss or volume change greater than 15 
percent. 


4.5.3 The material shall be such that the rubber 
components properties do not get impaired after the 
samples of the same have recovered completely to 
ambient temperatures from cooling to —20°C or heating 
to 65°C. For these tests, assembled VHPR is cooled to 
—20°C or heated to 65°C and maintained at these 
temperatures for 10 min and then kept in atmosphere 
to recover completely to ambient temperature of its 
own (not by induced heating or cooling). After 
recovery, the performance of the VHPR shall be re- 
verified. The results shall be within acceptable limits. 


4.5.4 The material shall meet the compression set 
requirements as in Annex G when subiected to 


IS 4786 : 2014 


compression set test in accordance with the method 
prescribed in Annex G. 


5 CONSTRUCTION AND WORKMANSHIP 


5.1 The VHPR shall be designed, manufactured and 
assembled in such a way as to provide satisfactory 
operation under the installation and service conditions 
specified by the manufacturer. The VHPR, including 
all the component parts, shall be mechanically strong, 
of sound construction and of a high degree of 
workmanship and finish. 


5.1.1 A VHPR shall be capable of resisting a fall on 
hard (concrete) surface from a height of 1 m and 
continuing to function satisfactorily, when tested as 
per 6 and 8.3. 


5.1.2 A typical VHPR schematic is shown in Fig. 1 
and Fig. 2 figure for illustration purpose only. Any other 
design as agreed to betvveen the purchaser and the 
manufacturer may be used provided it meets all 
requirements of this standard. The manufacturer shall 
specify VHPR based on the following: 


a) Gas — Propane, butane or LPG, 

b) Connections — inlet and outlet, 

c) Filter size (in microns), 

d) Operating temperature range in °C, 

e) Operating inlet pressure range in kPa 
(kgf/cm?), 

f) Delivered outlet pressure range with clean 
filter in kN/m? or gf/cm? or mm WC, 

g) Guaranteed flow rate in Nm”/h (with clean 
filter), and 

h) Outlet pressure range. 


5.2 Interchangeability 


The components of a VHPR shall be interchangeable 
with the corresponding components of any other VHPR 
of the same model and size. 


5.3 Screw Threads 


Unless otherwise specified, the threads on the inlet and 
outlet of the bodies of VHPRs fitted with screwed ends 
shall comply with the requirements of IS 551 
or IS 2643 or IS 4218 (Part 1 to Part 4) and shall have 
sufficient length of threads to provide clearance and 
prevent bottoming. 


5.4 Connections 


5.4.1 Where screwed connections are not used, the 
inlet of the VHPR shall be cast integrally as an 
inseparable part of the body or so fixed that it cannot 
be separated without damaging the body. The size and 
the profile of the inlet connection shall match the outlet 
end of the spring actuated self closing LPG cylinder

valve as per IS 8737, to achieve a leak proof coupled 
Joint without use of a resilient packing or washer or 
gasket as a part of the VHPR. However, the use of a 
gasket or packing shall be permitted so long as there is 
a leak proof joint with the valve, with the help of the 
gasket or packing as a part of the valve. 


5.4.1.1 Such VHPRs intended to be coupled to self 
closing valve by a quick coupling means, shall have 
an operating handle for manually turning ON and OFF 
the supply of gas. The ON and OFF positions shall be 
clearly marked and visible in recommended orientation 
of use. 


5.4.2 Where screwed connections are used for inlet 
of VHPR, the following shall apply: 


a) Screwed Ends — Where inlet connector is not 
fitted, the inlet of a VHPR with screwed ends 
shall comply with the requirements of 
IS 3224. 

b) Inlet Connector — Where used, any washer, 
connector and nut of a screwed inlet union 
shall comply with the applicable mating valve 
outlet connections as per IS 8737. 


5.4.3 Inlet Sealing 


If required by the customer, the VHPR shall incorporate 
a feature whereby the inlet passage to the VHPR shall 
remain sealed and shall not allow inflow of gas from 
the inlet, whenever the operating handle of the VHPR 
is brought to OFF position. The sealing shall remain 
effective at all inlet pressures in the range of the 
saturated vapour pressure of the gas at 65°C subject to 
a maximum of 1 667 kPa (17 kgf/cm”). A VHPR shall 
be considered to be confirming to the requirement when 
the leakage rate does not exceed 4 Nmm/?/s. 


5.4.4 The inlet connection shall be designed and 
manufactured to withstand a minimum hydrostatic 
pressure of 1.5 times the saturated vapour pressure of 
the gas at 65°C subject to a minimum of 1 770 kPa 
(18 kgf/cm?) for 2 min. 


5.4.5 The inlet connection shall also be capable of 
withstanding at ambient temperature the saturated 
vapour pressure at 65°C of the gas with which the 
VHPR is to be used. 


5.5 Outlet Connections 


The outlet of VHPR body shall have only internal 
threads, which shall be integral with the body, and shall 
comply with the requirements of IS 554. Incase external 
threads for fitment of outlet hose /pigtails are required, 
then brass connector provided with external threads 
shall be used. This connector shall comply with the 
requirements of IS 554 and shall be fitted in the body 
of the VHPR by using suitable retaining arrangement. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


5.6 Body and Cover 


5.6.1 The body and cover shall be strong enough to 
withstand the stress of connecting the VHPR to the 
cylinder valve or piping installation and to withstand 
normal stress imposed by service conditions, without 
developing leakage at joints, permanent deformation 
or other damage which might impair the serviceability 
of the VHPR. 


5.6.2 After machining and before finishing treatment 
(for example, painting), the body shall be non-porous. 
If pressure testing is used, the minimum gas or air 
pressure applied shall be 981 kPa (10 kgf/cm?). 


5.7 Valve Pad Fitting 


The valve pad (resilient) shall be so retained without 
use of adhesive that it cannot loosen or work out of 
position under service conditions. 


5.7.1 The inlet orifice and valve pad of the VHPR shall 
be protected by provision of a filter of suitable material 
compatible with LPG, of appropriate size of 
perforations that does not hamper flow of vapour but 
is yet effective against ingress of contaminating agents 
in the gas. Any acceptable arrangement meeting this 
requirement, as agreed between the manufacturer and 
the purchaser is also permitted. 


5.8 Vent 


The air vent hole (breather hole) above diaphragm 
space shall be of such a size and so located on the cover 
that: 


a) It does not easily become clogged/blocked, 

b) The accidental entry of foreign matter is 
minimized, and 

c) It would be difficult for an instrument inserted 
through the air vent hole to reach the 
diaphragm. 


NOTE — The purchaser may specify the provision of an insect 
screen over the vent hole. 


5.9 Outlet Pressure Adjustment Means 


The pressure adjustment means provided in the VHPR 
for varying the outlet pressure within the designed 
range of outlet pressures shall be simple and convenient 
to operate and once set by user shall remain ‘as set’, 
till next adjustment by user. Also, the adjustment 
means, shall be so constructed that turning it clockwise 
will increase the regulator outlet pressure and vice- 
versa. In case the adjustment utilizes change in spring 
load for varying the outlet pressure, it shall not be 
possible for the spring to get compressed to solid 
height, even by deliberate taking the adjustment to the 
extreme position of adjustment. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


It shall not be possible to set an operating outlet 
pressure greater than the declared outlet pressure for 
each type of VHPR tested as per the method given in 
Annex H. 


5.10 Relief Valves 


The inclusion of relief valves in VHPR construction is 
not recommended. 


5.11 Pressure Gauges 


Where an outlet pressure gauge is fitted as an integral 
part of the VHPR the maximum pressure (plus over 
pressure) which the gauge will withstand shall be at 
least 30 percent higher than the maximum outlet 
pressure setting that can be provided by the VHPR (see 
IS 3624). 


5.12 Strength of Connections 
5.12.1 Strength of the Connection/VHPR Assembly 


a) For Inlet Connections — Whether the fixing 
of the inlet connection onto the VHPR 
body is of the threaded or non-threaded 
type or in one piece, there shall be no 
damage or distortion that could affect the 
safety of the VHPR at the end of the tests 
given in 8.9 carried out with the following 
values: 

1) A torque of at least 30 Nm in both 
directions (see Table 1), 

2) A bending moment created by a force of 
400 N directed upvvards and vvhose 
application point is at the base of the 
outlet connection (see Table 3), and 

3) A tensile strength test of 2 000 N (see 
Table 1). 

b) For Outlet Connections — There shall be no 
damage or distortion of the outlet connection 
that could affect the safety of the VHPR at 
the end of the tests given in 7.7 carried out 
with the following values: 


1) A torque of at least 30 Nm in both 
directions (verification not required for 
freely rotating connections) (see Table 2); 
2) A bending moment of 10 Nm (not 
required for one piece connection) (see 
Table 2); 
3) A tensile strength test of 2 000 N (not 
required for one piece connection) (see 
Table 2). 
In addition, for freely rotating connections, the torque 
necessary for the rotation of the connection shall not 
be greater than 0.5 Nm at the end of all the tests carried 
out. 


5.12.2 Strength of VHPR Assembly When Fitted Onto 
its Cylinder Valve 


Following the tests given in 8.9, Table 3 carried out 
with the VHPR fitted to the installation as indicated in 
the instructions with the following values, there shall 
be no damage or distortion that could affect the safety 
of the VHPR: 


a) A torque in both directions of at least 30 Nm 
for threaded outlet connections. In addition, 
VHPRs with screwed unions vertically 
mounted onto the cylinder valve shall be 
subjected to a torque of at least 20 Nm in the 
VHPR plane, 

b) A bending moment created by a force of 400 
N directed upwards and whose application 
point is at the base of the outlet connection, 
and 

c) A tensile strength test of 500 N (verification 
not required for inlet connections screwed 
onto the cylinder valve). 


The mechanical strength required shall be ensured 
whatever the position of fixing of the VHPR onto the 
installation. 


6 SOUNDNESS 


6.1 A VHPR shall be considered to be leak tight when 
tested in accordance with 6.2 and 6.3 and if the leakage 
rate does not exceed 4 N mm?/s (The symbol ‘N’ 
indicates conversion to normal temperature and 
pressure conditions, NTP that is 760 mm of Hg pressure 
and 0°C). 


6.2 Inlet 


6.2.1 Those parts of the VHPR normally subjected to 
full cylinder pressure shall be leak tight at a minimum 
hydrostatic pressure as per 5.4.4 applied and held for 
a period of 2 min. 


6.2.2 Those parts of the VHPR normally subjected to 
full cylinder pressure shall also be tested for soundness 
at a pneumatic pressure not less than the pressure as 
per 5.4.5, applied and held for a period of not less than 
30 s and not more than 60 s. 


6.3 Outlet 


The completed VHPR shall be leak tight vvhen tested 
at 2.5 times the maximum outlet pressure obtainable 
from the VHPR applied through the outlet connection 
of a fully assembled VHPR and held for a period of 
not less than 30 s and not more than 60 s, after stability 
has been achieved. To get stability, adequate time is 
allovved betvveen introduction of test medium and the 
start of observation, so that the internal parts have 
attained balanced positions.

7 RANGE OF PRESSURE ADJUSTMENTS 


The designed range of pressure adjustments with the 
range of inlet pressures for obtaining the desired range 
of outlet pressures shall be as agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer. 


In the case of VHPR fitted with direct-reading 
calibrated means of adjustment, the calibrations shall 
be clear and legible. 


8 PERFORMANCE 
8.1 Test Gas 


The performance tests may be carried out with air or 
the gas for which the VHPR has been designed. In case

air is used as the test medium, due provision for a factor 
of conversion representing the flow of the appropriate 
gas for which the VHPR is designed shall be made 
(see IS 9798). 


8.2 Chatter 


A VHPR using the gas for which it is designed within 
its entire working range of inlet and outlet pressures 
shall not chatter or vibrate while it is being tested for 
performance. 


NOTE — It is improper to induce chatter by striking the VHPR 
severely or by using an output far in excess of the maximum 
rated capacity, conditions which may induce vibrations of the 
internal components and give a false impression of chatter. 


IS 4786 : 2014

Closing Valve or Manual Valve)

T and 72 are not applied if the regulator is freely turning on its cylinder valve. 


8.3 Orientation 


The VHPR shall be capable of being operated in all 
orientations, but the test shall be carried out with the 
VHPR in the recommended orientation. 


8.4 Outlet Pressure Measurement 


The pipe between the outlet of the VHPR and the outlet 
pressure gauge shall be of bore not less than the outlet 
of the VHPR and of length not so long as to create a 
significant, pressure drop. 


8.5 Flow Measurement 


Flow measurements shall be carried out using a direct 


indicating flowmeter (rotameter). Calibrated orifices 
may also be used. 


8.6 Pressure Deviations 


The VHPR shall be set so that it meets the performance 
requirements as per 8.7. 


8.7 Performance 


After setting as in 8.6 and with operating inlet pressure 
range not narrower than, the range given in Table 4, 
the outlet or delivery pressure shall not deviate from 
the setting by more than 20 percent with flows 
measured whilst rising from 10 percent to 100 percent 


of the specified test capacity. The static pressure shall 
not exceed the outlet pressure setting by more than 60 
percent for propane/LPG and 30 percent for butane. 
These requirements shall also be met after the VHPR 
has been exposed and has recovered from ambient 
temperature between —40°C and 65°C for propane and 
—20°C and 65°C for butane and mixtures of propane 
and butane. The Static (lock up) pressure shall be 
achieved within 60 s of cessation of flow. 


Table 4 Operating Inlet Pressure Range 
(Clause 8.7) 


SI No. Gas Operating Inlet Pressures 
kPa kgf/cm? 
(1) (2) (3) (4) 
1) Commercial propane 343 - 1 079 3.5 - 11

Hi) Commercial butane 78.5 - 314 0.8 - 3.2 


NOTE — The foregoing tests are intended as comparative tests, 
with the ‘specified test capacity’ laid down by the 
manufacturers. The maximum capacity will depend on operating 
circumstance.’ and the permissible pressure drop. 


8.8 The requirements of performance as given in 8.7 
shall also be satisfied before and after the subjecting 
the VHPR to the tests specified in 8.8.1, 8.8.2 and 8.8.3. 
Deviation in the initial setting, after these tests, is 
acceptable. 


8.8.1 Endurance Test 


When assessing a new design, a type approval test in 
accordance with Annex J shall be carried out. A fully 
assembled VHPR shall withstand a minimum of 5 000 
cycles applied to the regulating mechanism, of which 
500 cycles shall also include opening and closing 
operations of the operating handle, after which it shall 
be subjected to a soundness test as in 6.2.2 and 6.3 and 
performance as given in 8.7. 


8.8.2 Low Temperature Test 


The VHPR is exposed to a temperature of —20°C for a 
minimum period of 10 min for the completely 
assembled unit to attain this temperature. It is then 
removed and left exposed to ambient conditions, after 
which it is tested. The method of carrying out the test 
is elaborated in Annex D. 


8.8.2.1 Subsequent to the cooling, forced heating shall 
not be applied to bring back the VHPR to ambient 
temperature. 


8.8.2.2 Care shall be taken to avoid intrusion of fluid 
or moisture into the VHPR assembly during cooling 
and recovery. For this the outlet nozzle and the inlet 
and the breather hole may be plugged. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


8.8.3 High Temperature Test 


The VHPR is exposed to a temperature of 65°C for a 
minimum period of 10 min for the complete assembled 
unit to attain this temperature. It is then removed and 
left exposed to ambient conditions, after which it is 
tested. The method of carrying out the test is elaborated 
in Annex D. 


8.8.3.1 Subsequent to the heating, cooling shall not be 
applied to bring back the VHPR to ambient temperature. 


8.8.3.2 Care shall be taken to avoid intrusion of fluid 
or moisture into the VHPR assembly during heating 
and cooling. For this the outlet nozzle and the inlet 
and the breather hole may be plugged. 


8.9 Mechanical Strength of Connections 


Tests for mechanical strength shall be carried out using 
a dynamometric device with an accuracy of +5 percent. 
For the torque test, a system which neutralizes bending 
moments shall be used (if a torque wrench is used, it is 
desirable that this is double handed). The VHPR is fixed 
at the points indicated in the drawings given in 
Tables 1, 2 and 3. The duration of application of the 
torques and forces shall be 1 min. 


For the test carried out in accordance with Table 3. 


a) VHPRs with threaded connections, the 
connection shall be mounted on its valve as 
indicated in Table 3; and 

b) VHPRs with quick couplings, if the inlet 
connection rotates, the tensile strength test of 
15 N.m is not necessary; if the connection is 
locked in the original position, the VHPR shall 
be tested as such. 


In all cases the requirements of 5.13 shall be met. 


8.10 Inlet Sealing 


Verification of satisfactory sealing shall be done by 
the procedure described in Annex K. The inlet passage 
of the VHPR shall seal inflow of gas, when the inlet is 
subjected to pressures of 0.5 kgf/cm? and maximum 
working pressure of the gas and the operating handle 
of VHPR is brought to OFF position. 


8.10.1 The test shall be carried out for a minimum 
period of 30 s, for both pressure mentioned above. 


8.11 Drop Test 


This test shall be carried out to check that there is no 
cracking or damage to the VHPR when a steel ball of 
1 kg mass is dropped on the regulator from a height of 
1 m, with regulator resting on the flange or the ball 
falling on the flange, in special set up. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


Inspection shall be carried out to check that the 
regulator is leak tight when subjected to diaphragm 
leak test as specified in 6.3 after the above tests have 
been carried out. 


9 SEALING 


9.1 If the VHPR is permanently not crimped, the body 
and the cover of each VHPR shall be sealed to 
discourage interference with the internal mechanism 
as well as the setting. 


9.1.1 The manner of sealing shall be as agreed to 
between the purchaser and the manufacturer. 


10 CLASSIFICATION OF TESTS 


10.1 Type Tests 


The following shall constitute type tests out of the 
various requirements: 


a) Susceptibility to season cracking (see 4.1.1); 

b) Rubber material test (see 4.3, 4.4 and 4.5); 

c) Hydrostatic test (see 6.2.2); 

d) Endurance test (see 8.8.1); 

e) Low and high temperature tests (see 8.8.2 and 
8.8.3); and 

f) Mechanical strength of connection (see 8.9). 


10.2 Routine Tests 


The following shall constitute routine tests out of the 
various requirements: 


e) Soundness (see 6.2.2 and 6.3); and 
f) Chatter and performance (see 8.2 and 8.7). 
11 MARKING 


11.1 Each VHPR shall be legibly and indelibly marked 
with the following: 


a) Manufacturer’s name or trade-mark; 

b) The month and year of manufacturers, for 
example: 4/11 for April 2011; 

c) The number of this standard, followed by the 
letter ‘B’ indicating butane, “P” indicating 
propane or ‘LPG’ indicates mixtures of butane 
and propane; 

d) Any other marking agreed to between the 
purchaser and the manufacturer; 

e) Rated capacity in Nm*/h; and 

f) Direction for increase and decrease of the 


outlet pressure shall be clearly marked on 
adjustment means. 


11.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The VHPRs may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


11.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 
1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. 
The details of conditions under which the licence for 
the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


a) LPG compatibility (see 4.1); 
b) Finish (see 4.2.1)); 12 PACKING 
c) Dimensions (screw threads) (see 5.2, 5.3 and I . 
5.4.2): The VHPRs shall be so packed as to avoid damage in 
xa transit. The openings shall be sealed off to prevent the 
d) Inlet sealing (see 5.4.3 and 8.10): : 
entry of foreign matter.

ANNEX B 
(Clauses 4.3.2, 4.3.5, 4.4.2, 4.4.4 and 4.5.2) 
TEST GAS COMPOSITION 


The test gas is nominally 50 percent propane, 50 
percent propene. In practice this gas will conform to 
the following specification: 


A hydrocarbon mixture consisting 
predominantly of C, hydrocarbons 
approximating to 50/50 propane/propene. It 
shall have the following composition: 


a) The total content of propene shall not be less 


than 45 mols percent and not greater than 55 
mols percent; 


b) The total content of C, hydrocarbons shall not 
exceed 1 mol percent; and 
c) The total content of C, and higher, 


hydrocarbons shall not exceed 2 mols percent. 


Alternatively, liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) may be 
used as the test gas. 


ANNEX C 
(Clauses 4.3.3) 
BURSTING AND PULL OUT TEST OF DIAPHRAGM IN AN ASSEMBLED CONDITION 


C-1 GENERAL 


C-1.1 The test is designed to give a practical result on 
an assembled VHPR, and is intended as a simple check 
method which may be applied by the VHPR 
manufacturer to diaphragm material which will usually 
have been previously tested by some other method (for 
example, Mullin’s test) by the supplier. 


C-1.2 The test takes the form of a simple application 


of pressure (air or nitrogen is suitable) through the outlet 
connection to the underside of the diaphragm mounted 
in a VHPR in the fully assembled condition (that is as it 
would be supplied by the manufacturer to a buyer). 


C-2 TEST RIG 


C-2.1 The outlet of the assembled VHPR is connected 
to a supply of air or nitrogen. 


IS 4786 : 2014 


C-2.2 A gauge is incorporated in the test rig between 
the air or nitrogen supply and the VHPR to indicate 
the applied pressure. 


C-3 TEST METHOD 


C-3.1 The pressure is applied at approximately | kgf/ 
cm? per second up to the level specified in 4.3.3 and 
maintained for 120 s. 


ANNEX D 
(Clauses 8.8.2 and 8.8.3) 
LOW TEMPERATURE AND HIGH TEMPERATURE TEST 


D-1 DETERMINATION OF DIAPHRAGM 
FLEXIBILITY AT LOW TEMPERATURE 


D-1.1 Low Temperature Test 


D-1.1.1 A fully assembled VHPR, set as in 8.6 is placed 
in a sealed container and this container is immersed in 
a bath of any convenient fluid (namely, methanol or 
any suitable freezing mixture like salt + ice + calcium 
carbide) cooled to a steady temperature of —20°C and 
maintained at this temperature by some reliable means 
(by additions of dry ice). It is kept immersed long 
enough for the complete assembly to attain —20°C (10 
min) after which it is removed and exposed to the 
atmosphere so that the assembly returns to ambient 
conditions. It is then tested in accordance with 8.7 for 
performance. 


NOTE — Care should be taken to prevent the cooling fluid 
from entering the assembly or of moisture condensing inside. 


This may be avoided by ensuring that the sealed container is 
opened only after the assembly attains ambient conditions. 


D-1.2 High Temperature Test 


D-1.2.1 A fully assembled VHPR, set as in 8.6 is 
placed in a sealed container and this container is 
immersed in a bath of water heated to a steady 
temperature of 65°C. It is kept immersed long enough 
for the complete assembly to attain 65°C (10 min) after 
which it is removed and exposed to the atmosphere so 
that the assembly returns to ambient conditions. It is 
then tested in accordance with 8.7 for performance. 


NOTE — Care should be taken to prevent the bath water from 
entering the assembly, or of moisture forming inside. This may 
be avoided by ensuring that the sealed container is opened 
only after the assembly attains ambient conditions. Also air 
shall not be forced through the assembly in an attempt to 
accelerate cooling as this is likely to result in condensation of 
moisture inside the assembly.

(Clauses 4.3.5, 4.4.2 and 4.5.2)

The test is designed to evaluate the rubber material 
vis-a-vis its resistance to hydrocarbons.

ANNEX F 
(Clause 4.2.1.2) 
METHOD OF TEST FOR ADHESION OF PAINT 


A square measuring 12 to 15 mm sides shall be marked 
on plain surface (not having raised or sunk markings) 
of randomly selected specimen from the lot of painted 
or powder coated components. Cross lines at a distance 
of 1 to 1.5 mm and inched at approximately 120° angle 
with each other shall be described over the marked 


portion with a sharp pointed instrument. Cellulose tape 
shall be applied over this portion and left for 2 min 
after which is shall be Jerked free from the surface 
under test. If a more than 3 percent of the squares are 
ripped from the surface under test. The specimen shall 
be deemed to have failed test. 


ANNEX G 
(Clause 4.5.4) 
METHOD OF COMPRESSION SET TEST FOR RUBBER COMPONENT MATERIAL 


G-1 GENERAL 


The test is designed to difference between the original 
thickness of the test piece and that after recovery, 
expressed a percentage of the initial applied compression. 


G-2 APPARATUS AND TEST PIECES 
The apparatus shall as per 4 of IS 3400 (Part 10). The 
pieces for test shall be as per 5 of IS 3400 (Part 10). 


G-3 PROCEDURE 


Three mono-block test piece disc of (13 + 0.5) mm 
diameter and (6.3 + 0.3) mm thickness shall be tested 
as per 7 of IS 3400(Part 10) subjected to following 
conditions: 


a) Compression : 25 percent at (27 + 2°C) 

b) Duration of test : 168 + 2 h for valve pad and 
seal material and 24 + 0.5 h for diaphragm 

c) Test temperature : TÜ + 1°C 


G-4 CALCULATION 


Calculate the compression set expressed as a 


percentage of the initial deflection from the following 
formula: 


š İt

where

thickness of the test piece after recovery, in 
mm; and 


height of the spacer, in mm. 


The results for the three test pieces shall agree within 
5 percent of the mean compression set value; if they 
do not, the test shall be repeated.

ANNEX H 
(Clause 5.9) 
TEST ON OUTLET PRESSURE ADJUSTMENT MEANS 


H-1 DEFINITION 


The adjustment means, for varying the outlet pressure 
within the designed range of outlet pressures, is externally 
provided on the VHPR and is convenient to operate. 


H-2 TEST METHOD 
The inlet of the VHPR through a regulator of suitable 


capacity is connected to air supply of adequate capacity 
and pressure incorporating a flovvmeter. The outlet of 
the VHPR is connected to a T-connection vvith one end 
connected to a flow control valve and the other to a 
pressure indicating device. VVith inlet pressure set at 7 
kg/cm? the outlet pressure is adjusted to the maximum 
outlet pressure and flow is measured. 


ANNEX J 
(Clause 8.8.1) 
ENDURANCE TEST 


The inlet of the VHPR is connected, through an air 
pressure regulator, to air supply incorporating a 
flowmeter and solenoid operated pneumatic valves of 
adequate capacity. The 5 000 cycles test shall be carried 
out as follows: 


a) Keeping the operating handle in ON position 
and inlet pressure at 1.5 kgf/cm? for butane 
regulators and 7 kgf/cm? for LPG and propane 
regulators and 20 percent of the maximum 
flow rate the solenoid valves are operated for 
4500 cycles, for VHPR with operating handle 


or 5 000 cycles for VHPR without operating 
handle, such that during each cycle the 
diaphragm relaxes completely and closes its 
jet for at least 1 s. The length of each complete 
cycle shall be at least 5 s. 
b) Keeping all pressure and flow settings as 
above, the operating handle of the VHPR shall 
be operated for 500 cycles. 


At the end of each of the above tests soundness as per 
6.2.2 and 6.3 shall be ensured. 


ANNEX K 
(Clause 8.10) 


TEST FOR INLET SEALING 
(Only for VHPR having operating handle) 


K-1 DEFINITION 


The purpose of this test is to ensure that in case leakage 
occurs from the spindle of the valve due to some defect, 
the leaking gas is prevented from flowing into the 
VHPR when the VHPR operating handle has been 
turned OFF and effectively the user has made all efforts 
to contain the LPG. 


K-2 TEST METHOD 


A fully assembled VHPR is mounted on a valve (whose 


outlet matches with the inlet of the VHPR). The outlet 
of the VHPR is connected to a system (such as a 
differentometer, manometer, etc) which will indicate 
and measure leak, if any. Air/Gas is introduced into 
the VHPR inlet at highest and lowest operating 
pressures and the operating handle of VHPR is turned 
to ON position and occurrence of outflow confirmed. 
The operating handle of VHPR is then be turned OFF 
and rate of leakage, if any, is measured. 


IS 4786 : 2014

Bureau of Indian Standards 

BIS is a statutory institution established under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 to promote 
harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality certification of goods 
and attending to connected matters in the country. 

Copyright 

BIS has the copyright of all its publications. No part of these publications may be reproduced in any form 
without the prior permission in writing of BIS. This does not preclude the free use, in the course of 
implementing the standard, of necessary details, such as symbols and sizes, type or grade designations. 
Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director (Publications), BIS. 

Review of Indian Standards 

Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed 
periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are 
needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards 
should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of 


‘BIS Catalogue’ and ‘Standards : Monthly Additions’. 


This Indian Standard has been developed from Doc No.: MED 16 (1153).
